cards.front: How are insulin preparations grouped by onset and duration of action?
cards.back: **Rapid-acting** (lispro, aspart, glulisine): fastest onset, given with meals. **Short-acting**: **regular** insulin (also used IV in DKA). **Intermediate**: **NPH**. **Long-acting** (glargine, detemir, degludec): steady basal effect. Main adverse effect: **hypoglycemia**.
cards.back_pt: **Ação ultrarrápida** (lispro, asparte, glulisina): início mais rápido, aplicada às refeições. **Ação rápida**: insulina **regular** (também IV na CAD). **Ação intermediária**: **NPH**. **Ação prolongada** (glargina, detemir, degludeca): efeito basal estável. Principal efeito adverso: **hipoglicemia**.

cards.front: How does metformin lower blood glucose, and why does it not cause hypoglycemia?
cards.back: It activates **AMPK** and **decreases hepatic gluconeogenesis**. It does **not increase insulin release**, so on its own it causes no **hypoglycemia** and no **weight gain**. Common effects: **GI upset**; with long-term use, **vitamin B12 deficiency**.
cards.back_pt: Ativa a **AMPK** e **reduz a gliconeogênese hepática**. **Não aumenta a secreção de insulina**, então, isoladamente, não causa **hipoglicemia** nem **ganho de peso**. Efeitos comuns: **sintomas gastrointestinais**; com o uso prolongado, **deficiência de vitamina B12**.

cards.front: How do sulfonylureas and meglitinides increase insulin release?
cards.back: They **close ATP-sensitive K+ channels** on beta cells. The cell **depolarizes**, voltage-gated **Ca2+ channels** open, and insulin is released. They need working beta cells. **Meglitinides** (repaglinide, nateglinide) act on the same channel but are shorter-acting.
cards.back_pt: Esses fármacos **fecham os canais de K+ sensíveis a ATP** das células beta. A célula **despolariza**, os **canais de Ca2+** dependentes de voltagem se abrem e a insulina é liberada. Precisam de células beta funcionantes. As **glinidas** (repaglinida, nateglinida) atuam no mesmo canal, mas têm ação mais curta.

cards.front: How do thiazolidinediones work, and what are their main adverse effects?
cards.back: **Pioglitazone** activates **PPAR-gamma**, a nuclear receptor, and **increases insulin sensitivity** in fat and muscle. Adverse effects: **weight gain**, **fluid retention and edema** (avoid in heart failure), and **fractures**.
cards.back_pt: A **pioglitazona** ativa o **PPAR-gama**, um receptor nuclear, e **aumenta a sensibilidade à insulina** no tecido adiposo e no músculo. Efeitos adversos: **ganho de peso**, **retenção de líquido e edema** (evitar na insuficiência cardíaca) e **fraturas**.

cards.front: What do GLP-1 receptor agonists do, and what is their boxed warning?
cards.back: Exenatide, liraglutide, semaglutide: **glucose-dependent insulin release**, less glucagon, **slower gastric emptying** and satiety, so **weight loss**. Risks: nausea, **pancreatitis**. Boxed warning (long-acting agents, such as liraglutide and semaglutide): **thyroid C-cell tumors**; avoid with **medullary thyroid carcinoma** or **MEN2**.
cards.back_pt: Exenatida, liraglutida, semaglutida: **liberação de insulina dependente de glicose**, menos glucagon, **esvaziamento gástrico mais lento** e saciedade, com **perda de peso**. Riscos: náuseas, **pancreatite**. Advertência em destaque (*boxed warning*; agentes de ação prolongada, como liraglutida e semaglutida): **tumores de células C da tireoide**; evitar em caso de **carcinoma medular de tireoide** ou **NEM2**.

cards.front: How do propylthiouracil (PTU) and methimazole differ?
cards.back: Both block **thyroid peroxidase** (organification and coupling). **PTU** also blocks peripheral **T4-to-T3 conversion**, can cause **liver failure**, and is preferred in the **first trimester**. **Methimazole** is preferred otherwise; it is **teratogenic** in early pregnancy. Both: **agranulocytosis**.
cards.back_pt: Ambos bloqueiam a **tireoperoxidase** (organificação e acoplamento). A **PTU** também bloqueia a **conversão periférica de T4 em T3**, pode causar **insuficiência hepática** e é preferida no **primeiro trimestre**. O **metimazol** é preferido nas demais situações; é **teratogênico** no início da gestação. Ambos: **agranulocitose**.

cards.front: Why is it dangerous to stop long-term glucocorticoids suddenly?
cards.back: Exogenous steroids suppress **CRH and ACTH**, so the **zona fasciculata atrophies**. After abrupt withdrawal, the adrenals cannot make enough cortisol: **acute adrenal insufficiency** (hypotension, shock). Aldosterone is preserved because the **RAAS** still drives the zona glomerulosa. **Taper** instead.
cards.back_pt: Os corticoides exógenos suprimem **CRH e ACTH**, e a **zona fasciculada atrofia**. Após a suspensão abrupta, as adrenais não produzem cortisol suficiente: **insuficiência adrenal aguda** (hipotensão, choque). A aldosterona fica preservada, pois o **SRAA** continua estimulando a zona glomerulosa. Fazer **retirada gradual**.

cards.front: Why does teriparatide build bone, when high PTH in hyperparathyroidism causes bone loss?
cards.back: Teriparatide is a **PTH analog**. **Intermittent** exposure stimulates **osteoblasts** more than osteoclasts, so bone formation rises (**anabolic** effect). **Continuously** high PTH favors **osteoclast** resorption through **RANKL**.
cards.back_pt: A teriparatida é um **análogo do PTH**. A exposição **intermitente** estimula mais os **osteoblastos** que os osteoclastos, e a formação óssea aumenta (efeito **anabólico**). O PTH **continuamente** elevado favorece a reabsorção pelos **osteoclastos** via **RANKL**.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has had severe diarrhea and poor oral intake for 4 days. She takes one diabetes medication. She is now confused and breathing deeply and rapidly. Blood pressure is 92/58 mm Hg and pulse is 114/min. Serum studies show Na+ 138 mEq/L, Cl- 100 mEq/L, HCO3- 10 mEq/L, glucose 142 mg/dL, creatinine 3.1 mg/dL (baseline 1.0 mg/dL), and lactate markedly elevated. Serum ketones are negative. Arterial pH is 7.28 and PaCO2 is 22 mm Hg. What is the mechanism of action of the drug most likely responsible for her acid-base disorder?
choices: Closure of ATP-sensitive K+ channels in pancreatic beta cells
Activation of the nuclear receptor PPAR-gamma
Inhibition of SGLT2 in the proximal tubule
Activation of AMPK with decreased hepatic gluconeogenesis
Inhibition of alpha-glucosidase in the intestinal brush border
questions.explanation: She has a **high anion gap metabolic acidosis** (gap = 138 - 100 - 10 = 28) with high lactate after **acute kidney injury**. **Metformin** is cleared by the kidney; it accumulates and blocks hepatic use of lactate for gluconeogenesis, causing **lactic acidosis**. SGLT2 inhibitors are the most tempting choice because they cause **euglycemic ketoacidosis**, but her ketones are negative and her lactate is high.
questions.explanation_pt: Ela tem **acidose metabólica com ânion gap elevado** (gap = 138 - 100 - 10 = 28) e lactato alto após **lesão renal aguda**. A **metformina** é eliminada pelos rins; ela se acumula e bloqueia o uso hepático do lactato na gliconeogênese, causando **acidose lática**. Os iSGLT2 são a alternativa mais tentadora, pois causam **cetoacidose euglicêmica**, mas as cetonas dela são negativas e o lactato está alto.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman without diabetes has had three episodes of sweating, tremor and confusion over 2 months. Her husband has type 2 diabetes treated with glipizide. During an episode in the emergency department, her plasma glucose is 38 mg/dL, and her symptoms resolve with intravenous glucose. Blood drawn at that time shows a high insulin level and a high C-peptide level. Which test is the most appropriate next step to find the cause of her hypoglycemia?
choices: Serum screen for oral hypoglycemic drugs
CT scan of the abdomen to look for a pancreatic tumor
Serum anti-insulin antibody titer
Serum IGF-2 level
Morning serum cortisol level
questions.explanation: High insulin with **high C-peptide** means the insulin comes from her own beta cells, so injected insulin is unlikely. **Sulfonylureas** (glipizide is in the home) close beta-cell K-ATP channels and give the same lab pattern as an **insulinoma**, so a **sulfonylurea screen** comes first. Proinsulin is also high in both. Imaging for an insulinoma is the tempting choice, but it should follow a negative drug screen.
questions.explanation_pt: Insulina alta com **peptídeo C alto** indica que a insulina vem das próprias células beta, então insulina injetada é improvável. As **sulfonilureias** (há glipizida em casa) fecham os canais K-ATP das células beta e produzem o mesmo padrão laboratorial do **insulinoma**; por isso, a **pesquisa de sulfonilureias** vem primeiro. A pró-insulina também fica alta em ambos. A imagem para insulinoma é a escolha tentadora, mas deve vir depois de uma pesquisa de fármacos negativa.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with Graves disease started methimazole 6 weeks ago. She now has a 2-day history of fever, a very sore throat and painful mouth ulcers. Temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F) and pulse is 94/min. Her pharynx is red, and there is no posterior cervical lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly. Leukocyte count is 1,500/mm3 with 2% neutrophils. Hemoglobin and platelet count are normal. Free T4 is within the reference range. Which is the most likely cause of her findings?
choices: Thyroid storm
Infectious mononucleosis
Drug-induced aplastic anemia
Streptococcal pharyngitis in a patient with a normal marrow
Drug-induced agranulocytosis
questions.explanation: Fever and sore throat with an almost absent **neutrophil count** (about 30/mm3) in a patient on a **thionamide** is **agranulocytosis**. Stop the drug at once; patients on thionamides should get a **CBC** whenever fever or sore throat appears. **Aplastic anemia** is tempting, but it lowers all three cell lines, and her hemoglobin and platelets are normal. A normal free T4 and a modest pulse argue against thyroid storm.
questions.explanation_pt: Febre e dor de garganta com **contagem de neutrófilos** quase nula (cerca de 30/mm3) em uma paciente em uso de **tionamida** indicam **agranulocitose**. Suspender o fármaco imediatamente; pacientes em uso de tionamidas devem fazer **hemograma** sempre que surgirem febre ou dor de garganta. A **anemia aplásica** é tentadora, mas reduz as três linhagens, e a hemoglobina e as plaquetas dela estão normais. T4 livre normal e pulso pouco elevado falam contra crise tireotóxica.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old woman with osteoporosis started oral alendronate 3 weeks ago. She now has sharp retrosternal pain when she swallows. She takes the tablet at bedtime with a small sip of water and then lies down. Upper endoscopy shows a single discrete ulcer in the mid-esophagus with normal surrounding mucosa. Which instruction would most likely have prevented this problem?
choices: Take the tablet with a glass of milk and a calcium supplement
Take the tablet with a full glass of plain water and stay upright afterward
Take the tablet with the evening meal
Crush the tablet and mix it into soft food
Take the tablet together with an antacid
questions.explanation: This is **pill esophagitis**: a tablet that stays in the esophagus damages the mucosa directly. Bisphosphonates should be taken on an empty stomach with a **full glass of plain water**, and the patient should **stay upright** afterward. Taking it with milk, calcium, food or an **antacid** may seem protective, but these **bind the drug** and block its absorption without preventing the injury.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **esofagite medicamentosa** (*pill esophagitis*): o comprimido que fica parado no esôfago lesa diretamente a mucosa. Os bisfosfonatos devem ser tomados em jejum com um **copo cheio de água pura**, e o paciente deve **permanecer em pé ou sentado** depois. Tomar com leite, cálcio, comida ou **antiácido** pode parecer protetor, mas eles **se ligam ao fármaco** e bloqueiam sua absorção, sem prevenir a lesão.

notes.title: Endocrine drugs: diabetes, thyroid, steroids, bone and pituitary
notes.body_md:
## Diabetes

- **Insulin**: rapid (lispro, aspart, glulisine), short (regular), intermediate (NPH), long (glargine, detemir, degludec). Risks: **hypoglycemia**, **hypokalemia**, weight gain.
- **Metformin**: lowers **hepatic gluconeogenesis**; no hypoglycemia. GI upset, **B12 deficiency**, **lactic acidosis** (risk rises in kidney failure).
- **Sulfonylureas** (glipizide, glyburide): close beta-cell **K-ATP channels**; **hypoglycemia** with high C-peptide, weight gain. First-generation drugs (chlorpropamide): **disulfiram-like reaction**, SIADH-like hyponatremia. **Meglitinides**: same channel, shorter action.
- **Thiazolidinediones**: **PPAR-gamma**; weight gain, edema, heart failure, fractures.
- **GLP-1 agonists**: weight loss, pancreatitis, **thyroid C-cell tumor** warning. **DPP-4 inhibitors** (gliptins): raise the body's own GLP-1; weight neutral.
- **Acarbose, miglitol**: block intestinal **alpha-glucosidase**; flatulence, diarrhea.
- **Pramlintide**: **amylin** analog; slows gastric emptying, lowers glucagon.
- SGLT2 inhibitors: see renal pharmacology.

## Thyroid

- **Levothyroxine** (T4) replaces thyroid hormone; excess causes arrhythmias and bone loss.
- **PTU and methimazole**: block **thyroid peroxidase**; PTU also blocks peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion. **Agranulocytosis** (both), liver failure (PTU).
- **Radioactive iodine**: destroys thyroid tissue; contraindicated in pregnancy; can worsen **Graves eye disease**.
- **Potassium iodide**: quickly blocks hormone release.
- **Beta-blockers** (propranolol): control adrenergic symptoms.

## Steroids

- **Glucocorticoids** (hydrocortisone, prednisone, dexamethasone): Cushingoid features, **osteoporosis**, **hyperglycemia**, infections, adrenal suppression (taper them).
- **Fludrocortisone**: mineralocorticoid replacement in primary adrenal insufficiency.

## Bone

- **Bisphosphonates** (alendronate): inhibit osteoclast **farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase**; pill esophagitis, **osteonecrosis of the jaw**, **atypical femur fractures**.
- **Teriparatide**: intermittent PTH; anabolic. **Denosumab**: antibody against **RANKL**. **Raloxifene**: estrogen agonist in bone; raises **venous thrombosis** risk. **Calcitonin**: weak osteoclast inhibitor.
- Cinacalcet: see renal pharmacology.

## Pituitary and ADH

- **Cabergoline, bromocriptine**: **dopamine agonists** for prolactinoma.
- **Pegvisomant**: **GH receptor antagonist** for acromegaly. Octreotide: see GI pharmacology.
- **Desmopressin**: V2 agonist for central DI. ADH antagonists (tolvaptan, conivaptan): see renal pharmacology.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Diabetes

- **Insulina**: ultrarrápida (lispro, asparte, glulisina), rápida (regular), intermediária (NPH), prolongada (glargina, detemir, degludeca). Riscos: **hipoglicemia**, **hipocalemia**, ganho de peso.
- **Metformina**: reduz a **gliconeogênese hepática**; não causa hipoglicemia. Sintomas gastrointestinais, **deficiência de B12**, **acidose lática** (risco maior na insuficiência renal).
- **Sulfonilureias** (glipizida, glibenclamida): fecham os **canais K-ATP** da célula beta; **hipoglicemia** com peptídeo C alto, ganho de peso. Primeira geração (clorpropamida): **reação dissulfiram-símile**, hiponatremia semelhante à SIADH. **Glinidas**: mesmo canal, ação mais curta.
- **Tiazolidinedionas**: **PPAR-gama**; ganho de peso, edema, insuficiência cardíaca, fraturas.
- **Agonistas do GLP-1**: perda de peso, pancreatite, advertência sobre **tumor de células C da tireoide**. **Inibidores da DPP-4** (gliptinas): aumentam o GLP-1 do próprio organismo; neutros no peso.
- **Acarbose, miglitol**: bloqueiam a **alfa-glicosidase** intestinal; flatulência, diarreia.
- **Pranlintida**: análogo da **amilina**; retarda o esvaziamento gástrico, reduz o glucagon.
- Inibidores de SGLT2: ver farmacologia renal.

## Tireoide

- **Levotiroxina** (T4) repõe o hormônio tireoidiano; o excesso causa arritmias e perda óssea.
- **PTU e metimazol**: bloqueiam a **tireoperoxidase**; a PTU também bloqueia a conversão periférica de T4 em T3. **Agranulocitose** (ambos), insuficiência hepática (PTU).
- **Iodo radioativo**: destrói o tecido tireoidiano; contraindicado na gestação; pode piorar a **oftalmopatia de Graves**.
- **Iodeto de potássio**: bloqueia rapidamente a liberação hormonal.
- **Betabloqueadores** (propranolol): controlam os sintomas adrenérgicos.

## Corticoides

- **Glicocorticoides** (hidrocortisona, prednisona, dexametasona): aspecto cushingoide, **osteoporose**, **hiperglicemia**, infecções, supressão adrenal (retirada gradual).
- **Fludrocortisona**: reposição mineralocorticoide na insuficiência adrenal primária.

## Osso

- **Bisfosfonatos** (alendronato): inibem a **farnesil pirofosfato sintase** do osteoclasto; esofagite medicamentosa, **osteonecrose da mandíbula**, **fraturas atípicas de fêmur**.
- **Teriparatida**: PTH intermitente; anabólica. **Denosumabe**: anticorpo contra o **RANKL**. **Raloxifeno**: agonista estrogênico no osso; aumenta o risco de **trombose venosa**. **Calcitonina**: inibidor fraco dos osteoclastos.
- Cinacalcete: ver farmacologia renal.

## Hipófise e ADH

- **Cabergolina, bromocriptina**: **agonistas dopaminérgicos** no prolactinoma.
- **Pegvisomanto**: **antagonista do receptor de GH** na acromegalia. Octreotida: ver farmacologia gastrointestinal.
- **Desmopressina**: agonista V2 no DI central. Antagonistas do ADH (tolvaptana, conivaptana): ver farmacologia renal.
